assign.request: Make server.js boot-test a changed Server/ tree as a candidate child on a spare port before swapping the live child, never wedge, and survive a cold start into a broken tree. Prove eight ugly cases with scratch breakage on PORT=8143.
assign.now: reading run.js and every plugin for boot-time side effects
steps: Read the incident, server-self, run.js and every plugin for boot-time side effects
Design boot-test-and-swap plus the never-wedge watchdog in a scratch copy of server.js
Guard Directory.js and LiveReload.js for BOOT_TEST; confirm Whisper.js already skips
Prove the eight ugly cases on PORT=8143 with scratch-only breakage
Copy the proven server.js into the shared tree in one write; boot and curl it before anyone else's restart

log.msg: Boot-time side effects found by reading run.js and every plugin: only three things touch anything shared at boot - Whisper.js (already skips: OWNER_FACING is false whenever PORT is set and not 80, so a candidate on a spare port never spawns it), Directory.js (rebuilds public/directory.json + public/framework/directory.json unconditionally in initialize()), and LiveReload.js (polls/writes the shared .reload-hold.json via Hold.prune() on every listening server). Added one BOOT_TEST guard line to each of the latter two. Both node --check clean; booted Server/run.js directly on a private port 8143 with the two new guard lines in place (BOOT_TEST unset, so both behave exactly as before) - real HTTP 200, directory.json still rebuilds normally. Confirmed the owner's :80 and mastermind's :8123 both still answer 200 after this Server/ save reached them.

First full proof run (5 fails) traced to two real bugs plus one environment surprise. Bug 1: the HANGS scratch case used bare `await new Promise(() => {})`, which Node treats as an unsettled top-level await with nothing else keeping the event loop alive and exits it with code 13 almost immediately - it never actually hung, so the deadline path was never exercised; fixed by adding a real setInterval that keeps the loop open. Bug 2: node_modules was completely empty (0 packages) at some point mid-task - not caused by this task, gitignored, shared across every agent in this repo - every fresh boot (candidate or live) was failing on Cannot find package express. Ran npm install (71 packages restored, express confirmed resolvable); confirmed the owner's :80 and mastermind's :8123 stayed up throughout (they were already running in memory, unaffected by the missing files on disk) and are still 200 now. Re-running the eight-case harness.

decision.about: how server.js proves a Server/ change boots before it can touch the live child

options.say: fork a CANDIDATE on an OS-assigned free port with PORT=<spare> and BOOT_TEST=1, poll its own / for a real HTTP 200 with an 8s deadline racing its exit event; pass -> kill the candidate then swap the live child exactly as before; fail -> kill the candidate, leave the live child untouched, print the candidate's last output, write .server-boot-failed.json {at, files, error} at the repo root

leave server.js as-is and keep telling every minion to boot its own Server/ save before writing it (what the incident audit rejected - it already said this in the same sentence as the outage warning and the outage happened anyway)

decision.because: the incident's own audit named this exact shape as change 1, the highest-ranked fix; parsing was already checked three ways (node --check, the syntax-guard hook, the old pre-restart check) and booting was checked nowhere - this closes that gap mechanically instead of by habit.

decision.about: what a candidate must not do that a normal boot does

options.say: BOOT_TEST=1 is a flag a candidate's own environment carries; each side-effecting plugin checks it in one line - Directory.js skips its unconditional directory.json rebuild, LiveReload.js skips ever polling/writing the shared .reload-hold.json. Whisper.js needed no change: it already only starts when PORT is unset or 80, which a spare candidate port never is - confirmed by reading it, not assumed

decision.because: reading run.js and every plugin end to end found exactly these three boot-time side effects that touch anything shared; nothing else writes a file or binds an exclusive resource at boot (everything else in Ask.js/Start.js/Runtime.js/AILogs.js only writes inside a per-request RPC handler, never touched by a plain GET / boot-test).

decision.about: the second bug from the same incident - restart() waited forever for an exit event from an already-dead child

options.say: kill_and_wait() always resolves within a deadline (exit event, or taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F as the escalation); a generation counter lets a new restart() cancel an in-flight boot test instead of running two; a live child that dies after truly booting is respawned at once, one that dies inside its own first second is treated as broken and waits for a real change (not a timer, so a cold start into a broken tree cannot crash-loop); a backstop timer boots a live child if nothing is running and nothing is in flight

decision.because: the exact wedge (restarting stuck true forever) cannot recur by construction once every wait has a deadline - proved directly in cases d/e/g/h, not just reasoned about.

log.msg: Correction: the three decision lines just above are mistimed 21:35 - typed from memory off a stale UTC timestamp I had just been reading (a .server-boot-failed.json Z-suffixed value from a test run) instead of reading the real clock, exactly the trap new-task's skill names. Real local time at that point was about 16:34-16:35. Content of those decisions is correct, only the at field drifted; noting it here rather than rewriting an append-only log.

Eight-case proof, PORT=8143, SCRATCH breakage only (public/framework/ai/2026-09-19/server-boot-test/scratch/breakable.js + a test-only TEST_EXTRA_WATCH_DIR/TEST_EXTRA_MODULE pair server.js honours only when set). All eight PASS on the final proof.mjs run against the exact file later copied to server.js. (a) throws at import: live answered 200 on every 200ms poll across the whole episode (zero failures), .server-boot-failed.json written, block printed. (b) fix: one boot test, one swap, downtime ~163ms, failure file cleared. (c) hangs at boot: the real 8s deadline fires (a setInterval keeps the scratch module's event loop alive - a bare unsettled top-level await just exits Node at once, a real bug in my FIRST test attempt, not the supervisor), live untouched. (d) kill live child while idle: back on its own, ~230ms (first attempt showed a false failure - I was killing it inside its own 1s boot-grace window, a test timing bug, not a supervisor bug, fixed by waiting past it). (e) kill then save (the incident's exact state): a server came back within ~1.1s. (f) three saves 100ms apart: one boot test, one swap. (g) cold start into a broken scratch module: stays up, 'did not boot' logged exactly once (not spamming), boots ~1-1.1s after the fix lands. (h) Ctrl+C mid-boot-test: zero node processes left - proved with a real Windows console Ctrl+C event (GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent via a small PowerShell/Win32 helper, sigint-mid-boot-test.ps1 in the session scratchpad) because child.kill('SIGINT') from a separate Node process does NOT invoke a target's process.on('SIGINT') handler on Windows - confirmed on a bare test child first (it exited but its handler never ran) before trusting any SIGINT result from the real supervisor. Two harness bugs found and fixed along the way, both in my own proof script not the supervisor: pidAlive() always returned true regardless of the actual check (never inspected the captured output), and case (d)'s premature kill inside the boot-grace window. Owner's :80 and mastermind's :8123 polled/curled after every phase of this work and never dipped.

assign.outcome:
**`server.js` now proves a `Server/` change boots on a spare port before it can touch the live site — all eight ugly cases proved on `PORT=8143`.**

On a real change, a CANDIDATE forks on a spare port with `BOOT_TEST=1` and waits up to 8s for a real HTTP 200; only then does the live child get killed and the new one swapped in (the live gap is just the swap — measured ~150–250ms). On any failure the live child is never touched, the candidate's last output is printed, and `.server-boot-failed.json` at the repo root says why. Every kill is now deadline-bounded so the supervisor can never wedge again — the exact second bug from today's outage — and a cold start into an already-broken tree stays up and waits for a fixing change instead of crash-looping.

Two plugins needed one guarding line each so a candidate never touches shared state: `Server/plugins/Directory.js` (skips the `directory.json` rebuild) and `Server/plugins/SocketServer/LiveReload.js` (skips the reload-hold lock). `Server/plugins/Whisper.js` needed nothing — confirmed it already only starts for the owner-facing server.

**Proof, 8/8 pass**, downtime in ms — (a) throws at import: 0ms, live answered 200 on every poll; (b) fix: ~163ms; (c) hangs at boot: the real 8s deadline fires, live untouched; (d) kill the live child while idle: ~230ms; (e) kill then save (the incident's exact state): ~1.1s, no wedge; (f) three saves 100ms apart: one boot test, one swap; (g) cold start into a broken tree: stays up, boots ~1.1s after the fix lands; (h) Ctrl+C mid-boot-test: zero orphan processes — proved with a real Windows console Ctrl+C event, since Node's own `child.kill("SIGINT")` does not invoke a target's handler on Windows (confirmed on a bare test child first).

**To get it:** it is safe to restart the owner's `:80` and the mastermind's `:8123` by hand any time now — this exact file has been boot-tested repeatedly on a private port. Saving it into the shared tree just now did not change either already-running supervisor (each keeps its old in-memory code until restarted by hand); it only restarted their *child*, using the unchanged `Server/run.js`, and both stayed up throughout (polled before, during and after).

**Left:** `node_modules` was found completely empty mid-task — unrelated to this task, shared and gitignored, likely another agent's concurrent install — ran `npm install` to restore it (71 packages, `package.json`/`package-lock.json` unchanged) since it threatened every agent's dev server, not just this proof; who emptied it was not investigated further. `.server-boot-failed.json` is written only by the boot-test path, not the cold-start path — a deliberate scope choice, in the task log.
